questions.q: Which digits should come in place * and $, respectively, if the number 72864*$ is divisible by both 8 and 5?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: Unitary Scaling (Divisibility Rules) & Successive Change (Checking options)
Pen-Free Observation: Number divisible by 8 means last 3 digits must be divisible by 8. Divisible by 5 means last digit must be 0 or 5.
Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): For divisibility by 5, $ must be 0 or 5. For 8, it must be even, so $ = 0. Last 3 digits = 4*0. Check options: 440 is divisible by 8 (55*8). So * = 4.
Mathematically :-
\text{Divisible by 5 } \Rightarrow \text{Last digit} = 0 \text{ or } 5 \\ \text{Divisible by 8 } \Rightarrow \text{Last 3 digits} \, (4*0) \text{ must be divisible by 8} \\ \text{Checking options: } 440 \div 8 = 55 \\ \text{So } * = 4, \$ = 0
Method 2 (Concept Builder): Apply divisibility rules. 5: last digit 0 or 5. 8: number must be even, so 5 is out, thus $=0. Now 4*0 must be divisible by 8. Test * values from options. 440 works.
Exam Takeaway: Ninja method (option checking) is fastest.
RuleCondition
Divisibility by 5Last digit 0 or 5
Divisibility by 8Last 3 digits divisible by 8

questions.q:
The given table shows the number of soaps sold by four different companies in 4 different months.
Month/CompanyMayJuneJulyAugust
P1924178018201490
Q1540124516482450
R2035148513501650
S1736185514701180
The total number of soaps sold by companies Q and S together in May, is what percentage more than the number of soaps sold by company P in July?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: Unitary Scaling (Percentage Calculation)
Pen-Free Observation: Add Q (May) and S (May) = 1540 + 1736 = 3276. P (July) = 1820. Difference = 1456. 1456 is 4/5 of 1820 (since 1820 * 4/5 = 1456). So 80%.
Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Directly see difference: 3276 - 1820 = 1456. 1456/1820 = 0.8 = 80%.
Mathematically :-
\text{Sum (Q+S in May)} = 1540 + 1736 = 3276 \\ \text{Difference} = 3276 - 1820 = 1456 \\ \text{Percentage} = \frac{1456}{1820} \times 100 = 80\%
Method 2 (Concept Builder): Calculate sum, then subtract to find the difference, then divide by base (P in July) and multiply by 100.
Exam Takeaway: Direct difference method is fastest.
FormulaPercentage Increase
Percentage More\frac{\text{Difference}}{\text{Base}} \times 100

questions.q: In a triangle PQR, S is a point on the side QR such that PS⊥QR, then which of the following options is true?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: Cross-Product Method (Equating common terms from Pythagoras)
Pen-Free Observation: PS is perpendicular, so two right triangles are formed (PSQ and PSR). Apply Pythagoras to both, then equate the PS^2 terms.
Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Directly equate PS^2 from both triangles: PQ^2 - QS^2 = PR^2 - SR^2. Rearrange to get PR^2 + QS^2 = PQ^2 + SR^2.
Mathematically :-
\text{In } \triangle PQS: \, PS^2 = PQ^2 - QS^2 \\ \text{In } \triangle PRS: \, PS^2 = PR^2 - SR^2 \\ \Rightarrow PQ^2 - QS^2 = PR^2 - SR^2 \\ \Rightarrow PR^2 + QS^2 = PQ^2 + SR^2
Method 2 (Concept Builder): Apply Pythagoras theorem to both right triangles. Since PS is common, equate the values of PS^2 to get the relation.
Exam Takeaway: Equating the common perpendicular is the key.
TrianglePythagoras
PQSPQ^2 = PS^2 + QS^2
PRSPR^2 = PS^2 + SR^2

Core Conceptual Tool: Unitary Scaling (Basic Arithmetic - BODMAS)
Pen-Free Observation: Innermost brackets first. 14.5 - 13.5 = 1. Then work outward.
Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Start from inside: 14.5 - 13.5 = 1. Then 5 - 1 = 4. Then 7 - 4 = 3. Then 3 - 3 = 0. Finally 15.5 - 0 = 15.5.
Mathematically :-
15.5 - [3 - {7 - (5 - 1)}] \\ = 15.5 - [3 - {7 - 4}] \\ = 15.5 - [3 - 3] \\ = 15.5 - 0 \\ = 15.5
Method 2 (Concept Builder): Follow the order of operations: Parentheses, Brackets, then addition/subtraction.
Exam Takeaway: Always solve innermost bracket first.

questions.q: The incomes of P, Q and R are in the ratio 10 : 12 : 9 and their expenditures are in the ratio 12 : 15 : 8. If Q saves 25% of his income, then what is the ratio of the savings of P, Q and R?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: Unitary Scaling (Using two independent variables) & Cross-Product Method
Pen-Free Observation: Q saves 25%, so Q's expenditure is 75% of his income. That gives the link between income and expenditure variables.
Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Let incomes be 10x, 12x, 9x and expenditures be 12y, 15y, 8y. Q's saving: 12x - 15y = 25% of 12x = 3x. So 9x = 15y, thus y = (3/5)x. Now calculate savings: P = 10x - 12y = 10x - 36x/5 = 14x/5. Q = 12x - 9x = 3x = 15x/5. R = 9x - 8y = 9x - 24x/5 = 21x/5. Ratio = 14:15:21.
Mathematically :-
\text{Let Income} = 10x, 12x, 9x \\ \text{Let Expenditure} = 12y, 15y, 8y \\ Q: 12x - 15y = \frac{1}{4} \times 12x = 3x \\ \Rightarrow 9x = 15y \Rightarrow y = \frac{3}{5}x \\ \text{P Savings} = 10x - 12y = 10x - 12(\frac{3x}{5}) = \frac{14x}{5} \\ \text{Q Savings} = 12x - 15y = 12x - 9x = 3x = \frac{15x}{5} \\ \text{R Savings} = 9x - 8y = 9x - 8(\frac{3x}{5}) = \frac{21x}{5} \\ \text{Ratio} = 14 : 15 : 21
Method 2 (Concept Builder): Use two variables for income and expenditure. Use the given saving condition to find the relation between the variables. Then substitute to find individual savings.
Exam Takeaway: Linking the two ratios via the given saving percentage is the key.
PersonSavings
P14x/5
Q15x/5
R21x/5

questions.q:
The classification of 100 students based on the marks obtained by them in English and Mathematics in an examination is given in the table below. Study the table and answer the question that follows.

MATHEMATICS3236581100

If at least 40% marks in Mathematics are required for pursuing higher studies in Mathematics, how many students will be eligible to pursue higher studies in Mathematics?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: Unitary Scaling (Reading Tabular Data)
Pen-Free Observation: 40% of 50 marks = 20 marks. So we need the number of students who scored '20 and above' in Mathematics.
Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Directly read the table: In Mathematics row, under '20 and above', the number is 65.
Mathematically :-
40\% \text{ of } 50 = 20 \text{ marks} \\ \text{Look at '20 and above' column in Mathematics row} \\ = 65
Method 2 (Concept Builder): Calculate the cutoff marks (40% of 50 = 20). Then find the corresponding column in the table for Mathematics and read the value.
Exam Takeaway: This is a simple data interpretation question. Just know how to read a cumulative frequency table.

questions.q: In triangles ABC and DEF, AB = FD and ∠A = ∠D. The two triangles are congruent by SAS criterion if:
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: Cross-Product Method (Logical Mapping of Sides)
Pen-Free Observation: SAS requires two sides and the included angle. We have AB = FD and ∠A = ∠D. For angle A, the sides are AB and AC. For angle D, the sides are FD and DE. So we need AC = DE.
Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Check the options. Option 4 (AC = DE) is the only one that completes the SAS condition.
Mathematically :-
\text{SAS Criterion: } AB = FD, \angle A = \angle D, AC = DE
Method 2 (Concept Builder): Map the vertices: A ↔ D, B ↔ F, C ↔ E. Thus AB corresponds to DF (given FD), AC corresponds to DE, and BC corresponds to EF. For SAS, we need AC = DE.
Exam Takeaway: Carefully map the correspondence of vertices.

questions.q: Two pipes, A and B, can fill a tank in 10 minutes and 20 minutes, respectively. The pipe C can empty the tank in 30 minutes. All the three pipes are opened at a time in the beginning. However, pipe C is closed 2 minutes before the tank is filled. In what time, will the tank be full (in minutes)?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: Unitary Scaling (LCM Method for Time & Work)
Pen-Free Observation: Total work = LCM(10, 20, 30) = 60 units. Efficiencies: A = +6, B = +3, C = -2. C is closed for last 2 min, so during those 2 min, only A and B work (eff = 9).
Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Let total time be x. Work done by A and B for x minutes + work done by C for (x-2) minutes = 60. 6x + 3x - 2(x-2) = 60. 9x - 2x + 4 = 60. 7x = 56, x = 8.
Mathematically :-
\text{Total Work} = LCM(10, 20, 30) = 60 \\ \text{A} = 6, \text{B} = 3, \text{C} = -2 \\ \text{Let time} = x \text{ minutes} \\ 6x + 3x - 2(x - 2) = 60 \\ 9x - 2x + 4 = 60 \\ 7x = 56 \Rightarrow x = 8
Method 2 (Concept Builder): Use the LCM method to find efficiencies. Then set up the equation based on the time each pipe works. Pipe C works for (total time - 2) minutes.
Exam Takeaway: Using LCM avoids fractions and speeds up the process.
PipeTimeEfficiency
A10+6
B20+3
C30-2

questions.q: A payment of ₹120 is made with ₹10, ₹5 and ₹2 coins. A total of 25 coins are used. Which of the following is the number of ₹10 coins used in the payment?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: Cross-Product Method (Using Base Value & Extra Amount)
Pen-Free Observation: If all coins were ₹2, total = 25*2 = ₹50. We need ₹120, so extra = ₹70. Each ₹10 coin gives +8, each ₹5 coin gives +3. We need 8x + 3y = 70.
Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Check options for x (₹10 coins). If x=8, then 8*8 + 3y = 70 => 64 + 3y = 70 => 3y = 6 => y=2. Valid.
Mathematically :-
\text{Let x = ₹10 coins, y = ₹5 coins, z = ₹2 coins} \\ x + y + z = 25 \\ 10x + 5y + 2z = 120 \\ \text{Multiply first eq by 2: } 2x + 2y + 2z = 50 \\ \text{Subtract: } 8x + 3y = 70 \\ \text{Test x=8: } 64 + 3y = 70 \Rightarrow y=2 \text{ (valid)}
Method 2 (Concept Builder): Set up two equations. Eliminate z to get a linear equation in x and y. Check each option to see which gives an integer value for y.
Exam Takeaway: Option checking is the fastest way to solve such Diophantine equations.

questions.q: If 28.9 : x :: x : 36.1, and x > 0, then find the value of x.
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: Unitary Scaling (Mean Proportional)
Pen-Free Observation: For a continued proportion, x is the mean proportional. x = √(a*b). Here a=28.9 and b=36.1. Product is (289/10)*(361/10). √(289)=17, √(361)=19.
Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): x = √(28.9 * 36.1) = √(289*361 / 100) = (17*19)/10 = 323/10 = 32.3.
Mathematically :-
\text{x} = \sqrt{a \times b} \\ = \sqrt{28.9 \times 36.1} \\ = \sqrt{\frac{289}{10} \times \frac{361}{10}} \\ = \frac{17 \times 19}{10} \\ = 32.3
Method 2 (Concept Builder): Use the property of proportions: product of means = product of extremes. x*x = 28.9 * 36.1. Take square root.
Exam Takeaway: Recognize a continued proportion and apply the mean proportional formula directly.
ConceptFormula
Mean Proportionalb = √(a*c)

questions.q:
Study the given pie chart carefully and answer the question that follows.
The given pie chart shows the number of successful start-ups in different sectors in a particular year.

If the total number of successful start-ups is 2910, then find the number of start-ups in the education and agriculture sectors. (Neglect the decimal part.)
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: Unitary Scaling (Percentage Calculation from Pie Chart)
Pen-Free Observation: From the pie chart, Education = 24%, Agriculture = 12%. Sum = 36%. Calculate 36% of 2910. 36*2910 = 104760, divide by 100 = 1047.6. Neglect decimal => 1047.
Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): 36% of 2910 = (36/100)*2910 = 1047.6. Neglect decimal part = 1047.
Mathematically :-
\text{Total %} = 24\% + 12\% = 36\% \\ \text{Number} = \frac{36}{100} \times 2910 = 1047.6 \\ \text{Neglect decimal} = 1047
Method 2 (Concept Builder): Add the percentages from the chart, then apply the percentage formula to the total.
Exam Takeaway: Read the chart carefully and follow the instruction to neglect the decimal part.

questions.q: The height of a cylinder is 20 cm. The lateral surface area is 1760 cm<sup>2</sup>. Its volume is:
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: Unitary Scaling (Formulas for Cylinder)
Pen-Free Observation: Volume = πr²h. Since π=22/7, the final volume must be divisible by 11. Check options for divisibility by 11. Only 12320 is divisible by 11.
Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Check divisibility by 11 for options. For 12320, (1+3+0) - (2+2) = 4 - 4 = 0. So it's divisible by 11. That's the answer.
Mathematically :-
\text{LSA} = 2\pi r h = 1760 \\ 2 \times \frac{22}{7} \times r \times 20 = 1760 \\ \frac{880}{7} r = 1760 \Rightarrow r = 14 \\ \text{Volume} = \pi r^2 h = \frac{22}{7} \times 14 \times 14 \times 20 = 12320
Method 2 (Concept Builder): Calculate the radius from LSA, then use it to find the volume.
Exam Takeaway: Use the π=22/7 property to quickly check options for divisibility by 11.
FormulaExpression
LSA2πrh
Volumeπr²h

questions.q: Raj divides ₹1,200 in the ratio 2 : 1 : 3 among three of his friends. The amount equal to the sum of three times the largest share and two times the smallest share is:
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: Unitary Scaling (Ratio Division)
Pen-Free Observation: Total parts = 2+1+3 = 6. Value of 1 part = 1200/6 = 200. Largest share (3 parts) = 600. Smallest share (1 part) = 200. Need 3*600 + 2*200 = 1800 + 400 = 2200.
Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): 3*3 + 2*1 = 11 parts. 11 * 200 = 2200.
Mathematically :-
\text{Total parts} = 6 \\ 1\text{ part} = 1200 \div 6 = 200 \\ \text{Required} = 3 \times 3 + 2 \times 1 = 11 \text{ parts} \\ 11 \times 200 = 2200
Method 2 (Concept Builder): Find the value of each part, then compute the required combination.
Exam Takeaway: Combine the required parts before multiplying to save time.

questions.q: A shopkeeper marked an article at ₹5,000. The shopkeeper allows successive discounts of 20%, 15% and 10%. The selling price of the article is:
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: Successive Change (Successive Discounts)
Pen-Free Observation: Convert discounts to fractions: 20% = 4/5, 15% = 17/20, 10% = 9/10. Multiply MP by these fractions.
Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): SP = 5000 * (4/5) * (17/20) * (9/10) = 5000 * (612/1000) = 3060.
Mathematically :-
\text{SP} = 5000 \times \frac{80}{100} \times \frac{85}{100} \times \frac{90}{100} \\ = 5000 \times \frac{4}{5} \times \frac{17}{20} \times \frac{9}{10} \\ = 5000 \times \frac{612}{1000} = 3060
Method 2 (Concept Builder): Apply successive discounts one by one. After 20% discount, price = 4000. After 15% discount, price = 4000 * 0.85 = 3400. After 10% discount, price = 3400 * 0.9 = 3060.
Exam Takeaway: Converting percentages to fractions and multiplying is faster than applying discounts step-by-step.

questions.q: The average of 12 numbers is 48. The average of the first 5 numbers is 45 and the average of next 4 numbers is 52. If the 10<sup>th</sup> number is 10 less than the 11<sup>th</sup> number and is 5 more than the 12<sup>th</sup> number, then the average of the 11<sup>th</sup> and 12<sup>th</sup> numbers is:
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: JSM/Deviation (Averages)
Pen-Free Observation: Total sum = 12*48 = 576. Sum of first 9 = 5*45 + 4*52 = 225 + 208 = 433. Sum of last 3 = 576 - 433 = 143. Let 12th = x, then 10th = x+5, 11th = x+15. Sum = 3x + 20 = 143 => x = 41. 11th = 56, 12th = 41. Avg = (56+41)/2 = 48.5.
Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Use net deviation. First 9 numbers from 48: 5*(45-48) + 4*(52-48) = -15 + 16 = +1. So last 3 sum = 3*48 - 1 = 143. Then solve for x.
Mathematically :-
\text{Sum of 12} = 576 \\ \text{Sum of first 9} = 5 \times 45 + 4 \times 52 = 433 \\ \text{Sum of last 3} = 576 - 433 = 143 \\ \text{Let 12th} = x \Rightarrow 10th = x+5, 11th = x+15 \\ x+5 + x+15 + x = 143 \Rightarrow 3x = 123 \Rightarrow x = 41 \\ 11th = 56, 12th = 41 \\ \text{Avg} = \frac{56+41}{2} = 48.5
Method 2 (Concept Builder): Compute total sum and sum of known groups, then find the sum of the remaining three. Set up equations to find the individual values.
Exam Takeaway: The net deviation method is very fast for these problems.

questions.q:
Find the value of the following expression.
\(\sqrt{\frac{1 + \sin \theta}{1 - \sin \theta}}\)
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: Cross-Product Method (Rationalization)
Pen-Free Observation: Multiply numerator and denominator by (1 + sin θ). Denominator becomes 1 - sin²θ = cos²θ. Numerator becomes (1 + sin θ)². Take square root: (1 + sin θ)/cos θ = sec θ + tan θ.
Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Directly rationalize and simplify.
Mathematically :-
\sqrt{\frac{1 + \sin\theta}{1 - \sin\theta}} \times \sqrt{\frac{1 + \sin\theta}{1 + \sin\theta}} \\ = \sqrt{\frac{(1 + \sin\theta)^2}{1 - \sin^2\theta}} \\ = \sqrt{\frac{(1 + \sin\theta)^2}{\cos^2\theta}} \\ = \frac{1 + \sin\theta}{\cos\theta} \\ = \sec\theta + \tan\theta
Method 2 (Concept Builder): Rationalize the denominator using the conjugate, then simplify using trigonometric identities.
Exam Takeaway: Recognizing the conjugate is the key to solving these problems quickly.

questions.q: \(\left( \frac{\sin \theta - 2 \sin^3 \theta}{2 \cos^3 \theta - \cos \theta} \right)^3 \frac{1}{\tan \theta} - \sec^2 \theta\) = ?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: Cross-Product Method (Trigonometric Identities)
Pen-Free Observation: Factor out sin θ from numerator and cos θ from denominator. The inner term becomes sin θ(1 - 2sin²θ) / cos θ(2cos²θ - 1). But 1 - 2sin²θ = cos 2θ and 2cos²θ - 1 = cos 2θ. So it simplifies to tan θ. Then the whole expression becomes tan³θ * (1/tan θ) - sec²θ = tan²θ - sec²θ = -1.
Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Substitute θ = 30°. Calculate: (sin30 - 2sin³30)/(2cos³30 - cos30) = (1/2 - 2*1/8)/(2*3√3/8 - √3/2) = (1/4)/(√3/4) = 1/√3. Cube = 1/(3√3). Times (1/tan30) = 1/(3√3) * √3 = 1/3. Minus sec²30 = 4/3. So 1/3 - 4/3 = -1.
Mathematically :-
\text{Put } \theta = 30^\circ \\ \Rightarrow \left( \frac{1/2 - 2(1/8)}{2(3\sqrt{3}/8) - \sqrt{3}/2} \right)^3 \times \sqrt{3} - \frac{4}{3} \\ = \left( \frac{1/4}{\sqrt{3}/4} \right)^3 \times \sqrt{3} - \frac{4}{3} \\ = \left( \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} \right)^3 \times \sqrt{3} - \frac{4}{3} \\ = \frac{1}{3\sqrt{3}} \times \sqrt{3} - \frac{4}{3} = \frac{1}{3} - \frac{4}{3} = -1
Method 2 (Concept Builder): Use the double angle formula to simplify. sin θ(1-2sin²θ) = sin θ cos 2θ. cos θ(2cos²θ-1) = cos θ cos 2θ. So the term becomes (tan θ)³. Then simplify using sec²θ - tan²θ = 1.
Exam Takeaway: Substituting a standard angle is the fastest way to solve such expressions.

questions.q: \(\text{Let } t = \frac{2}{5}, \text{ then the value of the expression } t^3 + \left( \frac{3}{5} \right)^3 + \frac{9}{5} t \text{ is:} \)
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: Successive Change (Algebraic Identity)
Pen-Free Observation: The expression is in the form of (a+b)³ = a³ + b³ + 3ab(a+b). Here a = t, b = 3/5. Also, t + 3/5 = 2/5 + 3/5 = 1. So the expression equals (1)³ = 1.
Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Substitute t = 2/5 and calculate directly: (2/5)³ + (3/5)³ + (9/5)*(2/5) = 8/125 + 27/125 + 18/25 = (8+27+90)/125 = 125/125 = 1.
Mathematically :-
\text{Substitute } t = \frac{2}{5} \\ \left(\frac{2}{5}\right)^3 + \left(\frac{3}{5}\right)^3 + \frac{9}{5}\times\frac{2}{5} \\ = \frac{8}{125} + \frac{27}{125} + \frac{18}{25} \\ = \frac{8+27+90}{125} = \frac{125}{125} = 1
Method 2 (Concept Builder): Recognize the identity (a+b)³. Since t + 3/5 = 1, the expression is directly (1)³ = 1.
Exam Takeaway: Recognizing the algebraic identity can save calculation time.

questions.q: M and N walk along a circular track. They start at 5:00 a.m. from the same point in the opposite directions. M and N walk at a speed of 5 rounds per hour and 2 rounds per hour, respectively. How many times will they cross each other before 6.30 a.m. on the same day?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: Unitary Scaling (Relative Speed in Circular Motion)
Pen-Free Observation: Opposite directions => relative speed = sum of speeds = 5 + 2 = 7 rounds/hr. Time duration = 1.5 hours. Total crossings = 7 * 1.5 = 10.5. Since a crossing occurs for each full lap, we take the integer part => 10.
Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Relative speed = 7 rounds/hr. Time = 1.5 hrs. Crossings = 7 * 1.5 = 10.5 => 10.
Mathematically :-
\text{Relative speed} = 5 + 2 = 7 \text{ rounds/hr} \\ \text{Time} = 1.5 \text{ hours} \\ \text{Crossings} = 7 \times 1.5 = 10.5 \\ \text{Taking integer part} = 10
Method 2 (Concept Builder): In opposite directions, the number of crossings in 't' hours is equal to the product of relative speed and time, rounded down to the nearest integer if not exact.
Exam Takeaway: For opposite directions, add speeds. For same direction, subtract speeds.

questions.q: Two circles C₁ and C₂ touch each other externally. The radius of C₁ = 16 cm and the radius of C₂ = 8 cm. Find the length (in cm) of their common tangent.
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: Unitary Scaling (Direct Common Tangent Formula)
Pen-Free Observation: For externally touching circles, the direct common tangent length = 2√(R*r). Here R=16, r=8. 2√(16*8) = 2√128 = 2*8√2 = 16√2.
Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Apply the formula directly: DCT = 2√(16*8) = 16√2.
Mathematically :-
\text{DCT} = 2\sqrt{R \times r} \\ = 2\sqrt{16 \times 8} = 2\sqrt{128} \\ = 2 \times 8\sqrt{2} = 16\sqrt{2}
Method 2 (Concept Builder): Use the full formula: DCT = √(d² - (R-r)²). Here d = R+r = 24. So DCT = √(24² - 8²) = √(576 - 64) = √512 = 16√2.
Exam Takeaway: When circles touch externally, the DCT formula simplifies to 2√(R*r).

questions.q: If x + 1/x = 15, then the value of (7x<sup>2</sup> - 9x + 7) / (x<sup>2</sup> - x + 1) is:
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: Cross-Product Method (Divide by x)
Pen-Free Observation: Divide both numerator and denominator by x. This transforms the expression into a form that directly uses the given value of x + 1/x.
Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Expression = [7(x + 1/x) - 9] / [(x + 1/x) - 1] = [7*15 - 9] / [15 - 1] = [105 - 9] / 14 = 96/14 = 48/7.
Mathematically :-
\text{Divide by } x: \\ \frac{7x - 9 + 7/x}{x - 1 + 1/x} = \frac{7(x + 1/x) - 9}{(x + 1/x) - 1} \\ \text{Substitute } x + 1/x = 15: \\ = \frac{7(15) - 9}{15 - 1} = \frac{105 - 9}{14} = \frac{96}{14} = \frac{48}{7}
Method 2 (Concept Builder): Take x common from numerator and denominator, cancel it, and then substitute the value.
Exam Takeaway: Always look for the possibility of dividing by x when you have an expression like (ax² + bx + c)/(dx² + ex + f) and a condition like x + 1/x.

questions.q:
Study the given table and answer the question that follows.
The given table shows the production of different types of refrigerators in a company.

In which of the given year(s) was the production of B type refrigerator closest to its average production over the given years?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: JSM/Deviation (Averages)
Pen-Free Observation: Average of B = (1800+1890+1910+1940+1960)/5 = 9500/5 = 1900. Now check which year's value is closest to 1900. 2012: |1890-1900|=10. 2013: |1910-1900|=10. Both have the smallest difference.
Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Calculate average. Then find the minimum absolute difference. 1890 and 1910 are both 10 away from 1900.
Mathematically :-
\text{Average} = \frac{1800+1890+1910+1940+1960}{5} = 1900 \\ \text{Difference for 2012} = |1890-1900| = 10 \\ \text{Difference for 2013} = |1910-1900| = 10 \\ \text{Both have minimum difference}
Method 2 (Concept Builder): Calculate the average, then compute the absolute difference for each year, and select the year(s) with the smallest difference.
Exam Takeaway: This is a simple average calculation. Just be careful with the differences.

questions.q: The measures of the three angles of a triangle are in the ratio 17 : 13 : 15. Find the positive difference between the greatest and the smallest of these three angles.
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: Unitary Scaling (Angle Sum Property)
Pen-Free Observation: Sum of ratios = 17+13+15 = 45. 45 parts = 180°, so 1 part = 4°. Difference between greatest (17) and smallest (13) = 4 parts. 4 * 4° = 16°.
Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): 1 part = 180/45 = 4°. Difference = (17-13)*4 = 16°.
Mathematically :-
\text{Total parts} = 45 \\ 1\text{ part} = \frac{180}{45} = 4^\circ \\ \text{Difference} = (17-13) \times 4 = 16^\circ
Method 2 (Concept Builder): Find the value of each part, then multiply by the difference in ratio parts.
Exam Takeaway: For ratio-based angle problems, find the value of one unit first.

questions.q: If 2cosec<sup>2</sup>θ + 3cot<sup>2</sup>θ = 17, then the value of 'θ' when 0° ≤ θ ≤ 90° is:
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: Successive Change (Trigonometric Identities)
Pen-Free Observation: Use the identity cosec²θ = 1 + cot²θ. Substitute this into the equation.
Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): 2(1 + cot²θ) + 3cot²θ = 17 => 2 + 5cot²θ = 17 => 5cot²θ = 15 => cot²θ = 3 => cotθ = √3 => θ = 30°.
Mathematically :-
\text{cosec}^2\theta = 1 + \cot^2\theta \\ 2(1 + \cot^2\theta) + 3\cot^2\theta = 17 \\ 2 + 2\cot^2\theta + 3\cot^2\theta = 17 \\ 5\cot^2\theta = 15 \Rightarrow \cot^2\theta = 3 \\ \cot\theta = \sqrt{3} \Rightarrow \theta = 30^\circ
Method 2 (Concept Builder): Substitute the identity, simplify to find cot²θ, then determine θ.
Exam Takeaway: Knowing the basic identities is essential for such problems.

questions.q: A certain sum of money becomes seven times itself when invested at a certain rate of simple interest, in 14 years. How much time (in years, rounded off to 2 decimal places) will it take to become 18 times itself at the same rate?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: Unitary Scaling (Simple Interest Multiples)
Pen-Free Observation: For SI, if a sum becomes n times in T years, then the interest earned is (n-1) times the principal. The time required to become 18 times is directly proportional to (18-1) = 17. Since it becomes 7 times (interest = 6 times) in 14 years, the rate is such that 6 times principal is earned in 14 years. For 17 times principal, time = (17/6)*14 = 39.67.
Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): T₂ = T₁ * (n₂ - 1)/(n₁ - 1) = 14 * (18-1)/(7-1) = 14 * 17/6 = 119/3 = 39.67.
Mathematically :-
\text{T}_2 = \text{T}_1 \times \frac{(n_2 - 1)}{(n_1 - 1)} \\ = 14 \times \frac{18-1}{7-1} = 14 \times \frac{17}{6} \\ = \frac{238}{6} = 39.666... \approx 39.67
Method 2 (Concept Builder): Calculate the rate first from the first condition, then use it to find the time for the second condition.
Exam Takeaway: For SI, the time is proportional to (n-1). Use the direct formula to save time.
